newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: IPOs only relief in weak Singapore share market.
newsitem.headline: IPOs only relief in weak Singapore share market.

text.p: Singapore shares slid on Monday with falls in a range of heavyweight stocks as foreign institutions continued to sell.
In the absence of positive news for most stocks, interest focused on a couple of recent listings, Delifrance Asia, which debuted on Monday, and Labroy Marine, which listed on Friday.
Both soared above their issue prices, dominating volume.

The benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) closed down 20.29 points at 2,044.23. Turnover was a healthy 153.89 million shares but Delifrance and Labroy took more than 55 million of this total. Gainers led losers by 215 to 102.

"It doesn't look very good, does it?" complained one local broker. "Institutions are net sellers of this market. They say they are looking for a time to buy but are concerned there doesn't seem to be a bottom yet."
Labroy topped the actives list with 30.5 million shares sold. It ended 12 cents up at Singapore $0.95. Delifrance closed its first day at 97 cents, up from its IPO sale price of 78.
Among the losers were drinks firm Fraser & Neave, which closed down 50 cents at S$13.50.
